policy: Static entries authorize only a deliberately transcoded H.264 Main, yuv420p, SDR, 1080p30 plus AAC-LC stereo baseline. Bounded Portico Web bands may deliver that exact baseline through Portico's managed HLS player; this is not a claim of native browser HLS support. Rich codecs, HDR, Dolby Vision, multichannel, passthrough and object audio require authenticated runtime or native evidence.

references.versionBounds: 120-159; unknown versions use the same progressive-only codec floor
references.claim: Codec support and smooth/power-efficient decode are runtime questions; bounded Portico Web entries authorize only the managed H.264/AAC HLS baseline and do not claim native HLS, HDR, HEVC, AV1, or hardware decode.
references.limitations: OS codec installation, GPU, driver, build flags and MSE implementation vary.

references.claim: H.264 playback is supported through platform or software decode paths, but an Edge version does not establish native HLS or optional codecs.
references.limitations: Windows codec extensions, hardware acceleration and GPU drivers change the effective tuple.

references.claim: Effective H.264/AAC playback depends on operating-system codec availability; Firefox version alone does not authorize HLS or optional formats.
references.limitations: Distribution packaging and OS codecs vary, especially on Linux.

references.claim: Apple frameworks natively support HLS; the authoring specification supports H.264 and AAC stereo and WebVTT delivery.
references.limitations: HEVC, AV1, HDR, Dolby Vision and multichannel/output-route support varies by hardware and attached output.

references.claim: Media3 supports progressive MP4/M4A/MP3 and HLS MPEG-TS or fMP4 with WebVTT; elementary-stream decode remains platform-dependent.
references.limitations: Media3 delegates sample decoding to Android platform decoders by default, so OS version does not prove a device decoder.

references.versionBounds: Fire OS 7-8 and 14; other/Vega versions use conservative fallback
references.claim: Published Fire TV model specifications include H.264/AAC playback at or above Portico's baseline.
references.limitations: Fire OS version is not a device model; codec, HDR, resolution and audio-route capabilities vary materially by model. Vega OS is a separate runtime.

references.versionBounds: Roku OS 11-14; 15.x remains beta/unbounded until reviewed
references.claim: Roku documents MP4 H.264/AAC and HLS delivery; the static tuple remains below documented codec ceilings.
references.limitations: Codec/profile ceilings, multichannel AAC, HDR, Dolby Vision, captions and audio output vary by Roku model. Roku OS 15.3 was beta at review time.

references.versionBounds: No synthetic version band; device-independent fallback only
references.claim: Google documents H.264/AAC MP4 support across Cast receivers, with device-specific ceilings.
references.limitations: The submitted client version is not a Cast hardware generation. Codec/HDR/Dolby Vision capabilities differ across Chromecast, Nest, Google TV and custom receivers.
runtimeGaps: Cast canDisplayType for exact MIME/codec tuple

references.versionBounds: Samsung TV model years 2019-2026 (not Tizen API versions)
references.claim: Samsung's 2019 and 2026 TV specifications include H.264/AAC at or above the static baseline; Samsung documents HLS delivery.
references.limitations: Model year is only a coarse band. Panel resolution, HDR, Dolby formats, decoder limits, MSE versus AVPlay and regional audio support vary.

references.claim: LG's versioned TV specifications include MP4 H.264/AAC, HLS and WebVTT at or above the static baseline.
references.limitations: Ultra-HD, HDR and optional audio formats vary by model; webOS version does not identify panel or attached audio route.

references.claim: DLNA is kept progressive-only and low-confidence; no arbitrary renderer is assumed to support adaptive HLS.
references.limitations: A family label is not a renderer profile and cannot prove even the baseline tuple on every device.
